correctness.rationale: For p,q>=1 and p+q>=3, rotational block symmetry implies each unique optimizing ellipsoid has three scalar principal blocks. Inscription is equivalent to A<=a,C<=b,T<=b, giving John semiaxes a,b,b. Outer containment for each z²∈[0,b²] reduces to the two endpoint inequalities v+w<=1 and (1-t)v+h<=1. Maximizing v^p(1-v)^q(1-(1-t)v) gives one unique interior u from strict log-concavity and the quadratic derivative equation. The contact ridge saturates everywhere; two finite sign-orbit mixtures have zero mean and covariance I/d by the stationarity equation. The ratio decreases strictly in t, attaining the equal-radius endpoint and approaching, not attaining, its t↓0 upper bound. Independently verified derivative stationarity numerically for p,q=(2,1),(3,2),(1,4), four t each.

evidence: Güler–Gürtuna Section 8 treats a convex hull of sections; the present shape is an intersection of two cylinders, with a common saturating ridge.

value.rationale: This is a natural higher-dimensional Euclidean block generalization of the classical Steinmetz bicylinder, where p and q change the volume objective and contact distribution. A complete all-block-dimension radical optimizer, extremal contact locus and sharp ratio endpoints give a usable geometric classification, beyond a dimension-name substitution.

limitations: Only centered, orthogonal quadratic blocks and p+q>=3; no oblique/translated/general ellipsoidal sections.
Numerical stationarity checks are corroborative only, while strict concavity and contact covariance constitute proof.
